analyst_view.overall: Real Madrid are 2nd on a perfect 12 points under Jose Mourinho and came from behind to beat Celta 2-1 on Saturday, their ninth straight win, with Vinicius back from his domestic ban off the bench and Mbappe and Bellingham involved in the equaliser. PSV are 24th on 4 points and won 4-1 at NEC. Sergino Dest started at NEC but was taken off at half-time for an unstated reason, and midfielder Mauro Junior went off before the break with an apparent groin problem, so both are doubts the numbers do not know about. Schouten, Nagalo, Plea and Ouaissa remain long-term absentees (largely in PSV's recent form already), and Rodrygo is out for Madrid. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say a high 4.6 goals, from Madrid's strong recent scoring and PSV's attacking style under Bosz. PSV may lose Mauro Junior in midfield, which would weaken their defence, but it would also cost them some of their own threat, so the news points both ways. I stay at 4.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and already trim PSV (-6%) for their low recent count against strong defences. Madrid have their full front line available, which is already their normal state, so I see no reason to move. I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, close to both teams' usual rates. Vinicius's four-game ban was domestic and does not apply in Europe, and his card record is already in the numbers. No referee is named, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.1 shots, including Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+5%). If Mauro Junior misses out, PSV lose a key midfield runner and are likely to be pinned back more often, giving Madrid extra attempts. It is a small doubt, so I go only slightly higher, to about 31.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.8 on target, with Madrid's sharp recent finishing counted (+8%). Mbappe, Vinicius and Bellingham all look available, and PSV's attack scored four at NEC, so nothing new changes the accuracy picture. I stay at 12.8.
